the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Take a point r_2 of R_2 in the closure of a(R_1) and show it lies in a(R_1). First reduce by base change: pick a field extension k inside k' and a point r_2' of R'_2 adapted to (U, R_2, s_2, t_2, c_2) and r_2 as in the explain-points lemma; restrict both R_i via U' = Spec(k') to U = Spec(k), and let a' be the base change of a. The square with a' on top and a below is a fibre square, so the image of a' is the inverse image of the image of a under p_2 : R'_2 to R_2; by the restrict-groupoid-on-field lemma p_2 is surjective and open, so by the topology open-morphism quotient-topology lemma r_2' lies in the closure of a'(R'_1). Hence one may assume the maps k to kappa(r_2) induced by s_2 and t_2 are isomorphisms. In this case the move-point lemma applies and shows c(r_2, a(R_1)) is an open neighbourhood of r_2; since r_2 is in the closure of a(R_1), the intersection a(R_1) intersect c(r_2, a(R_1)) is nonempty; using the inverses of R_2 and R_1 this means r_2 lies in c_2(a(R_1), a(R_1)), which is contained in a(c_1(R_1, R_1)) = a(R_1), so r_2 in a(R_1) as desired.
